FT2NFDUMP(1)              BSD General Commands Manual             FT2NFDUMP(1)

NAME
     ft2nfdump — convert flow-tools files to nfdump format.

SYNOPSIS
     ft2nfdump [-r ftfile] -w nffile [-z=<compress>] [-j] [-y] [-E] [-c num]
     ft2nfdump [-hV]

DESCRIPTION
     ft2nfdump is the flow-tools converter program to read, convert and store
     netflow data, created with the flow-tools package. It works either as a
     pipe filter or reads flow-tools data directly from a file and exports nf‐
     dump data to a file.

     The options are as follows:

     -r ftfile
             Read the flow-tools netflow data from file ftfile If this argu‐
             ment is missing, ft2nfdump expects the data at stdin (pipe fil‐
             ter)

     -w nffile
             Writes netflow data to nffile

     -z=lzo  Compress flow files with LZO1X-1 compression. Fastest compres‐
             sion.

     -z=bz2  Compress flow files with bz2 compression. Slow but most effi‐
             cient. It is not recommended to use bz2 in a real time capturing.

     -z=lz4[:level]
             Compress flow files with LZ4 compression. Fast and efficient. Op‐
             tional level should be between 1..10 Changing the level results
             in smaller files but uses up more time to compress.

     -z=zstd[:level]
             Compress flow files with ZSTD compression. Fast and efficient.
             Optional level should be between 1..10 Changing the level results
             in smaller files but uses up more time to compress.

     -j      Legacy shorthand for -z=bz2.

     -y      Legacy shorthand for -z=lz4.

     -c num  Limit the number of flows to the first num flow records.

     -E      Additionally print flows to stdout This option allows you to
             check for the correct flow conversion and should not be needed
             for normal operation.

     -V      Print ft2nfdump version and exit.

     -h      Print help text to stdout and exit.

EXAMPLES
     To convert a flow tools file into nfdump format:
           % ft2nfdump -r <flow-tools-file> -z=lz4 -w <nfdump-file.nf>
           % nfdump -r <nfdump-file.nf>

RETURN VALUES
     ft2nfdump returns 0 on success and 255 otherwise.

SEE ALSO
     nfdump(1)
